The chapters and verses were defined in the middle ages to make it easier to make sure that everyone is on the same page (literally!) Even the titles were added -- sometimes you'll see Genesis called The First Book of Moses or even Moses I, with more variations.

"Agnostic: A person who believes..." That eliminates me right off the bat.
Maybe I should replace "believes" with "thinks", but that's just the dictionary definition I used

I'd say that "thinks" is just a somewhat diplomatic variation on "believes." It's the same basic thing in the long run though, and is exactly the opposite of the way I approach things. And it's just a bit disconcerting, because the way I approach things is exactly why, almost 40 years ago, I settled on the word "agnostic" as a self-descriptor.

Really the fundamental point, in my opinion, is that I don't waste my time and energy believing (or thinking) that this or that unknown thing is true or not true. In fact, I've never fully understood why people invest time and energy into believing one or another unproven assertion. I don't see the point. Ask me how big the universe is and I'll say, "I don't know." Ask me how life came to exist and I'll say "I don't know." Ask me if there's some manner of being who in some way caused the universe we perceive and/or the life within it to come into existence and I'll say "I don't know." Why? Because I don't know, and I see nothing to be gained from pretending that I do.

Eh... who knows. Maybe focusing on what one knows or doesn't know instead of what one believes or doesn't believe is such an uncommon approach to things that I'll have to cede "agnostic" to the believers as well. But I'd rather not.

That's what being agnostic is, not knowing, and believing that you can never know. It's just a matter of phrasing. But I see your point, but feel free to stick around; this isn't just for agnostics, but anyone that can contribute to discussion of agnosticism.

That's what being agnostic is, not knowing

Sort of. In point of fact, as far as this particular issue goes, nobody actually knows, so the case could be made that everybody is agnostic, which I'd say is self-evidently true, and therefore trite.

That's why I define an agnostic as one who simply admits to not knowing and lets it go at that, rather than weighing that trite universal lack of knowledge down with some additional, unnecessary and arguably irrational belief on the matter. I think that that's specifically what denotes an "agnostic" - not that the agnostic doesn't know, but that the agnostic accepts "I don't know" as his/her actual position on the matter, rather than freighting it with some additional belief.

and believing that you can never know.

I know that there are some who use the term in that manner, but I don't, for the above stated reasons. I think they're free to do so, but I won't allow them to force me to do so as well.

And more to the point, and particularly to that latter point, in almost 40 years of discussing the matter, I've encountered very, very few people who actually hold that position (in fact, most of those I've encountered who have insisted on that definition have been militant atheists who posited that definition so that they could erect a straw man in place of my own conception of "agnosticism"). Far and away, most of the self-described "agnostics" I've encountered have shared my own view of the matter - that "agnostic" isn't a belief at all, but rather a simple admission of an objective fact - that one, in fact, does not know.

this isn't just for agnostics,

Obviously what you mean is that it's not just for what you consider to be an agnostic. I would hope that that's the case.

but anyone that can contribute to discussion of agnosticism.

See... that's an interesting thing. As I said, I've called myself an "agnostic" - by which I mean exactly what the latin root means: "one who does not know" - for close to 40 years now. And really, in all that time, and in spite of the fact that I've spent more than 20 of those years posting on internet forums and all 40 of them talking to intelligent people, I've never really discussed agnosticism much at all. If appropriate, I just outline my view on the matter and why I call that view "agnostic," and if I'm talking to another who shares my position, there'll likely be that excited realization that we've both escaped the trap of belief and a bit of attention paid to the fact that "I don't know" is an objectively true claim, and... that's pretty much it. There's nothing about it that really needs to be discussed, since it's not a position of faith, so there's no need for justification or affirmation, so there's no need for all the rhetoric and arguments and attacks and other tactics that true believers use to prop up their faith. "Discussion" among those I count as agnostics tends to go something like:

"I just accept the fact that I don't know."

"Yep - me too. I just don't know, and that's fine."

"Yep."

"...."

"...."

If nothing else though, it should be interesting to see where this sub goes.
